# Benchmark

Measures whether the harness (AGENTS.md, hooks, skills, the tf-check MCP server
and the two sub-agents) makes the agent cheaper and more reliable than a plain
setup. The tasks and success criteria were written before any run (W2.8).

**Results: [results/report.md](results/report.md)**, generated by `make bench-report`
from `results/runs.csv`, `results/usage.csv` and `prices.csv`. No number in it is typed by hand.

## Method

- 4 tasks (`tasks/`) x 2 configurations (baseline, harness) x 2 runs = 16 runs.
- Every run starts from the git tag `bench-base-v1`, in a fresh Claude Code session,
  started with `make agent` (no AWS session, the agent's limited token), with the
  exact prompt from the task file. Same model for every run (`claude-opus-5-5`).
- Each configuration runs in its own copy of the repo, reset before every run by
  `make bench-setup CONFIG=harness|baseline` (`scripts/bench-setup.sh`):
  - **harness**: `~/code/aigt-bench-harness`, the repo as it is at the tag.
  - **baseline**: `~/code/aigt-bench-baseline`, the same commit with the agent config
    removed: `.claude/` (hooks, skills, sub-agents, settings), `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`
    and `.mcp.json`. Git is told to ignore those deletions (skip-worktree), so they
    never reach a commit or a pull request.
- CI is the same in both configurations: it is the referee, not part of the harness.
- After a run is recorded, its pull request is closed without merging, and its branch
  deleted. Nothing from a run reaches `main` or AWS.
- The tag is protected by a GitHub ruleset (`protect-bench-tags`): it cannot be moved
  or deleted.
- Order: round 1 alternates which configuration goes first per task; round 2 reverses it.

## What is recorded

| Metric | Source | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens (5 types) | `results/usage.csv`, by session ID | input, output, cache write 5 min, cache write 1 h, cache read; sub-agent logs are added to their session |
| Cost | `report.py` with `prices.csv` | tokens x list price per type; never a raw token sum (cache reads cost 5% of input) |
| Success | the task's criteria | every criterion holds, judged from the PR's plan and CI |
| First-pass CI | GitHub | all CI checks pass on the first push |
| CI pushes | GitHub | pushes until all checks pass |
| Stop-hook blocks | the session log | times the completion hook made the agent continue |
| Human interventions | the session log | messages from the human after the prompt |

One row per run goes into `results/runs.csv`, with the PR number. Numbers come from
logs and GitHub only, never from memory.

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `make usage REPO=<copy>` | reads a copy's Claude Code logs into `results/usage.csv` |
| `run_facts.py` | after a run: its session ID, pushes until CI green (only this PR's commits), stop-hook blocks; prints a draft row |
| `mutation_t4.sh` | T4 judge: breaks the s3_bucket module 5 ways in a throwaway worktree; the PR's tests must fail each time |
| `make bench-report` | builds `results/report.md`; fails on missing or inconsistent data |

How each task was judged: T1 and T2 from the PR diff and the CI plan (read with
`plan_summary`); T3 from the diff against the tag; T4 with `mutation_t4.sh`.

## What happened during the runs (2026-11-08 and 09)

- **Pilot, discarded:** in the first session all four prompts were pasted one after
  another, so later tasks had earlier ones in context. Its PRs (#39-#42) were closed
  and it is not in `runs.csv`. Rule since then: one task per fresh session.
- **Aborted attempt:** T1 harness run 1, attempt 1 lost its connection (PR #44, closed).
  The run was redone from a clean copy (PR #45).
- **Helper bug, fixed before analysis:** `run_facts.py` first counted pushes by branch
  name, and branch names were reused across PRs. It now counts only the PR's own
  commits; rows T1-h1, T2-h1 and T3-b1 were recounted. Success and cost were not affected.
- **Human interventions:** none in any of the 16 runs.

## Known limits

- 2 runs per cell: differences are indications, not statistically significant results.
- The agents can read this folder, including the success criteria.
- Account skills synced by Claude Code (`~/.claude/skills/synced`: xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf,
  docs, skill-creator, google-workspace, computer-use, chrome-browser, built-in-browser,
  morning, deep-research, import-memory) were present in **both** configurations. None is
  about Terraform.
- T2's task file expected risk level `low`; every T2 run was `medium`, because the
  s3_bucket module creates a bucket policy, which the risk gate counts as a permissions
  change. The task was not changed during the runs.
- `mutation_t4.sh` also counts a mutation as caught if Terraform cannot start. The
  unmutated module must pass first, and none of the 5 mutations breaks the file format.
- Stop-hook blocks are counted as distinct "attempt N" messages in the session's logs.
- T1-h2 (PR #52) derives the alarm threshold from the Lambda timeout. That it equals `8000`
  was judged from the agent's own test, which asserts `8000`, not checked by the owner in
  the plan output. The run counts as a failure anyway (criterion 4), so no result changes.
- Human interventions were counted by hand. Claude Code stores a sub-agent's final report
  as a "user" message in the session log, so an automatic count must skip those.
- Since PR #61 (2026-11-10), `main` has a newer `guard.yml` than the tag. GitHub refuses
  an agent push of a branch made from the tag (most likely because the agent token has
  no permission to change workflow files), so a new run from the tag would have to rebase
  on `main` first (agent-log entry 24). All 16 runs were before PR #61.
- Dollar cost is the API list price of the tokens on the date in `prices.csv`, not
  what a subscription charged.
- Usage rows written before W3.4 have one cache-write column; it is counted at the
  cheaper 5-minute price. No benchmark run is affected.
